partners.mechanism_chain: VCP (HGNC:12345) —DISRUPTS→ Ubiquitin-proteasome system (GO:0000985); VCP (HGNC:12345) —DISRUPTS→ Autophagy (GO:0006914); Ubiquitin-proteasome system (GO:0000985) —LEADS_TO→ Neurological impairment (HP:0001257); Autophagy (GO:0006914) —LEADS_TO→ Neurological impairment (HP:0001257); Autophagy (GO:0006914) —LEADS_TO→ Megaloblastic anemia (HP:0001890); MTR (HGNC:7477) —DISRUPTS→ Cobalamin (vitamin B12) (CHEBI:15360); Cobalamin (vitamin B12) (CHEBI:15360) —DECREASES→ Methionine (CHEBI:17888); Methionine (CHEBI:17888) —DECREASES→ Methylmalonic acid (CHEBI:25734); Methylmalonic acid (CHEBI:25734) —LEADS_TO→ Megaloblastic anemia (HP:0001890); VCP (HGNC:12345) —INCREASES→ Methylmalonic acid (CHEBI:25734). Mutations in VCP disrupt both the ubiquitin-proteasome system and autophagy, leading to the accumulation of misfolded proteins and cellular dysfunction, manifesting as FTD/ALS. Concurrently, VCP dysfunction can indirectly affect cobalamin metabolism, leading to methylmalonic acid accumulation and megaloblastic anemia, characteristic of cblG deficiency. The accumulation of methylmalonic acid can also contribute to neurological impairment. While MTR is also implicated in cblG, VCP's role in protein turnover provides a direct link to the neurodegenerative aspects of both diseases.
